advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wrap the ValueError-raising parse sites in _parse_batch_output (data.index / int(parts[2])) as RuntimeError, or add ValueError to the caught tuple in module_size_trend, so truncated batch output produces a categorized Unavailable reason.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py:317: `newline = data.index(b"\n", pos)` raises ValueError when no newline is present
src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py:325: `sha, size = parts[0], int(parts[2])` raises ValueError on a non-numeric size
src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py:369: `except (subprocess.SubprocessError, OSError, RuntimeError) as exc:` — ValueError is not in this tuple

Contrast: the batch parser deliberately raises RuntimeError for missing/malformed headers (lines 322,324) precisely so they are caught and categorized — the two ValueError sites are the inconsistent gap
advisory.finding: _parse_batch_output can raise ValueError (from data.index(b"\n", pos) when git output is truncated with no terminating newline, or from int(parts[2]) when the size field is non-numeric), but module_size_trend only catches (subprocess.SubprocessError, OSError, RuntimeError). A ValueError therefore bypasses _git_failure_reason categorization.
advisory.suggested_fix: In _parse_batch_output, guard the missing-newline and int() cases to raise RuntimeError (as the other malformed-header branches already do), or add ValueError to the except clause at git_metrics.py:369.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that drives a git failure at the blob-sampling stage (post-qualification) and asserts module_size_trend returns a categorized Unavailable.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py:367-370: try: samples = [_revision_sample(...) for index in indices] except (subprocess.SubprocessError, OSError, RuntimeError) as exc: return Unavailable(reason=_git_failure_reason(exc), ...)

test_oracle_git_history_metrics_return_specific_unavailable_reasons monkeypatches git_metrics._git (tests/unit/metrics/test_git_metrics_heldout.py:334), which raises in _qualified_history's rev-parse before any _revision_sample call — the sampling-stage handler is never reached.
ABSENCE: no test injects a failure into _blob_newline_counts / _revision_sample (e.g. a cat-file --batch failure after a valid qualified history) to drive the added except at line 369.
advisory.finding: The sampling-stage failure path in module_size_trend (catching a git error during per-revision blob reads and returning a categorized Unavailable) is never exercised; the only git-failure test monkeypatches _git, which fails inside _qualified_history before sampling begins, so the try/except at the sampling stage is untested.
scenarios: A cat-file --batch error or a corrupt/missing blob after qualification succeeds would exercise this handler in production, but no test confirms it yields Unavailable rather than an unhandled exception.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a unit test for _parse_batch_output asserting RuntimeError on a 'missing' blob line and on a malformed header.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/git_metrics.py:321-324: if len(parts) == 2 and parts[1] == "missing": raise RuntimeError(...); if len(parts) != 3: raise RuntimeError(...)

ABSENCE: no test in test_git_metrics.py or test_git_metrics_heldout.py feeds _parse_batch_output a 'missing' or malformed header; named uncovered input: batch stdout header b"<sha> missing\n" should raise RuntimeError.
advisory.finding: The _parse_batch_output error branches for a 'missing' blob and a malformed header (both added lines that raise RuntimeError) have no test coverage.
scenarios: Git returning a 'missing' object line (e.g. after a partial clone or corrupt object) would hit this raise; the behavior is asserted nowhere.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Batch the per-commit cap/tree reads in `_qualified_history` (e.g. a single `git cat-file --batch`/`--batch-all-objects` or a bulk `ls-tree` pass) instead of spawning 2-3 git processes per in-range commit.
evidence: `for sha, ts in in_range:` then `cap = _read_cap_at(repo_root, sha)` and `py_blobs = _py_blobs_at(repo_root, sha)` (git_metrics.py:256-266)
`_read_cap_at` runs `_git(repo_root, "ls-tree", sha, ...)` then `_git(repo_root, "cat-file", "-p", ...)` (git_metrics.py:200-202) — up to 2 subprocess spawns per commit
`_py_blobs_at` runs `_git(repo_root, "ls-tree", "-r", sha, ...)` (git_metrics.py:212) — a third subprocess spawn per commit
`_in_range` docstring: 'Filtering is done in-process rather than via git log --since/--until' (git_metrics.py:65-66), so with `since`/`until` None every reachable commit is processed
each `_git` call is a `subprocess.run(["git", *args], ... timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT)` with `_GIT_TIMEOUT = 300` (git_metrics.py:41-48, :26); the whole O(N) walk shares one timeout budget

By contrast `_blob_newline_counts` deliberately batches blob reads into one `git cat-file --batch` call (git_metrics.py, `_blob_newline_counts`), showing per-blob spawns were consciously avoided but the per-commit tree/cap reads were not
advisory.finding: `_qualified_history` issues 2-3 git subprocess invocations per in-range commit (`_read_cap_at`: `git ls-tree` + `git cat-file -p`; `_py_blobs_at`: `git ls-tree -r`) inside a loop over every date-filtered reachable commit. Since the date range is user-controlled and may be unbounded (both `since`/`until` can be None, and `_in_range` filters in-process so no `git log` narrowing occurs), the number of process forks grows linearly with repository history and can exhaust the 300s git timeout on a large repo before any sample is produced.
scenarios: `rebar metrics` run over a repository with thousands of commits in the requested (or default/unbounded) date range
A wide or open-ended `--since`/`--until` window that admits most of the repo's history

test_cap_change_events_reports_ordered_changes and the oracle both assert exactly one event; test_cap_change_events_empty_list asserts zero. Named uncovered input: caps 800 -> 900 -> 850 across three qualified revisions should yield events=[{from:800,to:900,...},{from:900,to:850,...}].
dropped.finding: cap_change_events is only tested with histories producing zero or exactly one cap-change event; the multi-event ordered-list behavior (three or more distinct adjacent caps yielding >1 event in order) is never asserted, so a regression in event ordering or accumulation across multiple changes would pass undetected.
scenarios: A refactor of the pairwise accumulation (e.g. accidentally emitting only the last change, or reversing order) would still pass the single-event tests.
